title: The Grateful Dead Live at Lakeland Civic Center on 1982-09-12
lineage: CD -> Samplitude Professional v11.2 -> Adobe Audition v1.5 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Reel -> Dat -> CD

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with good clarity (a little hiss and thin bass) captures a high‑energy show highlighted by a funky West LA, scorching “Might As Well” and an unforgettable “Playing in the Band.”
ai_review.review: The SBD source delivers a generally clean mix, though listeners note some hiss and a slightly recessed low end for Phil’s bass. Musically the concert is praised for its tight set flow, standout funk on West LA, powerful second‑set jams – especially “Might As Well,” “Playing in the Band,” and the seamless transition from “The Wheel” into “Morning Dew.” Overall the performance feels hot and inspired despite a few minor mix quirks.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4‑5 stars, highlighting strong playing and energetic set; recording is described as good with only modest hiss or mix imbalance, leading to a solid combined score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp overall sound with slight hiss; bass feels thin and Phil is low in the mix; Brent’s keyboards sit high and sometimes dominate; otherwise a clean SBD capture that is listenable.

poor_songs: Woman Are Smarter (average for some reviewers)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Concise, tight transitions with a fire‑filled second set; the band moves smoothly from funk‑y numbers into expansive jams and closes with a powerful Dew.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for being on fire, articulate, and handling “Might As Well” flawlessly; one reviewer notes his guitar is almost absent on “Greatest Story.”
band_member_comments.Phil: Frequently mentioned as low in the mix and lacking its usual fatness, though still audible.
band_member_comments.Bob: Generally described as spot‑on with inspired vocals; a few comments say he’s hard to hear due to mix balance.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent’s playing is highlighted as jazzy and “channeling Dave Grusin,” but his level in the mix is sometimes too high or uncomfortable on certain songs.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey & Bill receive strong praise for responsive, jazz‑like interplay, especially during “Playing in the Band.”
